name: design-detect-changed-files-by-role
prompt: /design-detect (git shows src/pricing.html and src/pricing.css changed: an without alt, a .badge with color #9a9a9a on background #fff, padding: 13px, and a :root that defines --color-text-muted: #6b6b6b while .note uses color: #6b6b6b)
expected_output: Runs the deterministic linter on the two changed files with --json and explains each finding under the owning role with concrete before/after fixes that reuse the project's existing tokens

assertions.name: runs-linter-json
assertions.description: runs node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/design-lint.js" --json on the changed files instead of judging the files by eye

assertions.name: groups-by-role
assertions.description: groups findings under role headings (UX Researcher for img-alt and contrast-aa, Design System Lead for spacing-grid and hardcoded-color)

assertions.name: cites-rule-and-line
assertions.description: names each rule id with its file and line number

assertions.name: contrast-fix
assertions.description: reports the .badge contrast as below 4.5:1 and proposes a darker text color that passes

assertions.name: reuses-token
assertions.description: suggests replacing #6b6b6b with var(--color-text-muted) rather than inventing a new token

assertions.name: errors-first
assertions.description: orders roles with errors before roles with only warnings and points to /design-review or /design-score for judgment calls

name: design-detect-nothing-to-lint
prompt: /design-detect (the only changed files in git are README.md and package.json)
expected_output: Says there is nothing to lint because no HTML, CSS or component files changed, and does not report a score

assertions.name: filters-extensions
assertions.description: filters the git change list to .html/.css/.scss/.jsx/.tsx/.vue/.svelte files

assertions.name: nothing-to-lint
assertions.description: states that there is nothing to lint

assertions.name: no-fake-score
assertions.description: does not report a 100/100 score or say all checks passed

assertions.name: suggests-next-step
assertions.description: suggests passing files explicitly (e.g. /design-detect src/index.html) if the user wanted a specific file checked

name: design-detect-ai-slop-cliches
prompt:
/design-detect src/landing.html (hero uses linear-gradient(135deg, #667eea, #764ba2), four cards with backdrop-filter: blur(12px), feature list items that start with 🚀 ✨ 🔒, and an

Unlock the power of your data

; .naksha/project.json has brand.primary #0f766e)
expected_output: Reports the slop-* findings as taste warnings owned by the Creative Director and Content Designer, explains why each pattern reads as generic, and proposes brand-led alternatives using the teal primary

assertions.name: flags-slop-rules
assertions.description: reports slop-gradient-hero, slop-glassmorphism, slop-emoji-bullets and slop-generic-copy

assertions.name: taste-not-defect
assertions.description: frames slop findings as warnings about generic taste rather than accessibility defects

assertions.name: brand-alternative
assertions.description: proposes a hero treatment derived from brand.primary #0f766e instead of the blue-violet gradient

assertions.name: emoji-a11y
assertions.description: explains that screen readers announce emoji names at the start of each list item and suggests list styling or aria-hidden SVG icons

assertions.name: concrete-copy
assertions.description: rewrites the headline as a concrete outcome but leaves the final wording to the user
